findings: The three richly framed main dormer assemblies, higher central crest and double/triple window groups retain the distinctive French neo-Renaissance composition of the 2016 municipal facade photograph and 1888 Salm elevation. These read clearly in the native gallery and actual canal-front scene.

Ground-floor composition remains intentionally asymmetric, with narrow central openings and the large right carriage entrance; horizontal stone bands, cornice and stoep railing reinforce the sandstone facade identity.

Current-state roof differs appropriately from the 1888 drawing: plain small intermediate roof windows are used and obsolete standing ridge-end figures are absent. The steep principal roof and restrained crest fit the photographed family.

Rear game view preserves the lower pitched rear house and surrounding garden/neighbor space. Source summaries establish independently low middle and rear roof zones; the review does not treat the small equipment/crest maximum as uniform building height.
No material facade, roof, native-scope or neighbor-retention failure found in the inspected evidence.
limitations: Sandstone color is warmer and relief more schematic than the weathered grey 2016 photo; flat-color relief conveys architectural grouping rather than individual carving.
Arched glazing heads, dormer scrolls, cornice carving and lantern details are simplified.
Actual front view trees partly obscure the ground floor; gallery and elevation supply a clear comparison of its asymmetric arrangement.
2016 is the inspected current-state facade photograph; no 2026 exterior image or surveyed facade dimensions were inspected. Rear fenestration and skylight placement remain approximate.
